content:
いま話題のAI『Genspark』を触ってみたけど、正直かなり衝撃でした！

特にアップデートされた「Ai Slides 5.0」。
AIでスライドを作るのもすごかったけど、AI Slides 5.0になりさらにやばい。
これ、ただのスライド生成AIじゃないです。

普通、プレゼン資料って、
・構成を考えて、
・流れを整理して、
・デザインを整えて、
・伝わる表現を作って、
・図解や見せ方を工夫して、
…つまり、めちゃくちゃ頭を使いますよね。

でもAi Slides 5.0は、
AIが対話形式で質問してくれて、それにどんどん答えていくだけで、かなり完成度の高い資料が出来上があります、マジでスゴイ！

しかも必要に応じて、
「参考URLありますか？」
「既存資料ありますか？」
って聞いてくれるから、貼るだけ・渡すだけで、さらにクオリティの高いクリエイティブが完成します。

実際に僕も、運営している『AGARU』のセミナー資料を作ってみたけど…

「え…、ナニコレ…これ自分で作るより分かりやすいかも…」
って普通に思ったし、ちょっと嫉妬しました（笑）

デザインもかなり洗練されてるし、
Skill「スキル」は設計したSlidesを再現できる再現性が高い。
これまで資料作成って、時間も気力も圧倒的に奪われる作業だったけど、

Ai Slides 5.0は、「考える負荷」そのものをかなり減らしてくれる感覚。

・本業の会議資料
・副業のセミナー
・営業提案、
・コンテンツ制作

たぶん全部に使える。

しかもGensparkって、AIを横断して使えるオールインワークスペースだから、タブを大量に開いて行ったり来たりする必要もない。
一流コンサル会社のアプローチ・ロジックを搭載していて、スキルを作る際に、いくつかの質問で結果物の質が半端ない。

これはもう、便利ツールというより「仕事の相棒」に近いかも（笑）

本業でも副業でも、
AI活用を一段引き上げたい人は、一回触ってみるといいです　↓　↓　↓

※有効期間は5月27日 9:00 〜 6月10日 9:00となります

The future of on-chain AI agents depends a lot on speed and smooth liquidity.

If transactions are slow or complicated, AI agents can easily miss good market opportunities.

That’s why the integration between @syra_agent and @QwertiAI is something worth paying attention to.

Qwerti’s White-label Widget is now fully integrated into the Syra platform, making it easier for users to buy and swap $SYRA directly from the website without stress.

No more complicated bridging.

No need to move between different platforms.

Everything can now be done in a few seconds with smooth multi-chain swaps directly on the site.

This makes the whole experience faster, cleaner, and easier for both new and experienced users.

To celebrate the integration, @QwertiAI is also launching a trading campaign for the community.

A total of 500,000 Qwerti Points will be shared among users trading $SYRA through the Syra website widget or the Qwerti app.

It’s a good opportunity for active traders to explore the platform while earning rewards at the same time.

Reward distribution will happen on Sunday, May 31st, 2026.

As AI and on-chain technology continue to grow, easy access to liquidity and fast transactions will become more important than ever. 

Integrations like this are helping make DeFi simpler, faster, and more user-friendly for everyone.

【12基のV100搭載！爆速で動く法務特化型ローカルLLMクラスターが凄い】

自前で12基のTesla V100（32GB）を搭載したモンスターマシンの運用事例が登場しました！

実務で活用するための高度な技術ポイントが凝縮されています。

・自己汚染の徹底管理
AIが生成した過去の誤情報を再び検索・参照しないよう、入力データを厳格に管理することが安定運用の鍵となります。

秘匿性の高い情報を安全かつ高速に処理する、士業DXの理想形ですね！🚀

content:
次世代推論モデル「GRAM」がAIの常識を覆す！
👉  https://t.co/auY4NzppXJ
ヨシュア・ベンジオ氏らが発表した最新研究「Generative Recursive Reasoning Models（GRAM）」が注目を集めています。

これまでのAIのように単に言葉を予測するのではなく、内部で「思考」を繰り返す仕組みが最大の特徴です。具体的には、内部の潜在状態を何度もアップデートして考えを深めたり、複数の思考プロセスをシミュレーションして最適なルートを探り当てたりすることが可能になります！

この技術が統合されれば、AIの論理的推論能力は飛躍的に向上します。複雑な意思決定の自動化や、高度な戦略立案を行う自律型エージェントの核として、ビジネス現場での活用が非常に期待されますね。🚀

title:
An AI agent got tricked into draining its own wallet, without touching a single line of code.

An attacker sent a free NFT to Grok's connected wallet. The NFT quietly escalated the wallet's permission
content:
An AI agent got tricked into draining its own wallet, without touching a single line of code.

An attacker sent a free NFT to Grok's connected wallet. The NFT quietly escalated the wallet's permissions. 

The attacker then posted a Morse code message on X, Grok decoded it, treated it as a legitimate command, and transferred $174,000.

If you're connecting an AI agent to a wallet: any token it receives and any text it reads online is a potential instruction. 

The bar for "input validation" just moved.

content:
➥ The next DeFi Summer might be agent-driven

Private inference probably was just the first breadcrumb for the AI crypto arc. Imo, the next bigger narrative might be agents actually using that trust layer to move money.

Once models can think privately, the next obvious bottleneck is letting them actually do things with money.

Crypto might be the only financial system built for that world, tbh.

AI agents can’t open bank accounts. But they can create wallets, sign transactions, hold stablecoins and interact with smart contracts instantly.

Internet money is already becoming the coordination layer for autonomous software.

→ private inference solved the trust layer
→ wallet infra solved identity
→ stablecoins solved settlement
→ x402 solved machine-to-machine payment
→ ERC-8004 brings on-chain identity and reputation for agent
→ DeFi becomes the execution environment

Some early data already showing autonomous trading agents reducing slippage ~30% while improving yields ~12% over manual strategies.

What happens when AI agents become the smarter interface sitting on top of all that flow?

Ngl, the vibes feel insanely DeFi summer coded.

Back then it was ERC20s, Uniswap, Compound, Aave, oracles, stablecoins, then liquidity mining.

Now it’s private inference, agent wallets, x402, ERC-8004, $Eliza, $Virtuals ACP, $Bankr, $VVV,..

If the narrative can’t go huge then why are Coinbase, Google, Stripe, AWS and other big names already building infra around it?

Some crypto infra forming around this narrative atm:

– $VVV | @AskVenice: bridge between private inference and agent fuel. Agents could become the largest users of private inference.

– $VIRTUAL | @virtuals_io: pushed $13.8B in DEX volume with ~40k agents deployed. Leading agent launchpad with real revenue and ACP standard adoption.

– $BNKR | @bankrbot: sitting at the intersection of every AI agent infra piece. Controls 69% launchpad market share on Base, printed $24.3M in fees.

– $SERV | @openservai: building fu

title: YouTube to begin automatically labeling AI videos
content: AI content creation tools like Google's new Omni model threaten to make reality even harder to discern from AI fantasy, but YouTube is taking an important step toward verifying video origins. After debuting wishy-washy AI content labeling in 2024, Google will begin using more prominent labeling for AI videos, and the site will no longer rely entirely on uploaders to divulge when they use AI tools to create a video. When YouTube first attempted to tackle the identification of AI videos in 2024, it was almost gratuitous. AI videos at the time nearly always outed themselves by looking bizarre or disjointed. In just a few years, AI models like Seedance, Runway, and Google's own Veo have raised the bar for realism and consistency in AI video— the spaghetti is more accurate than ever. Recognizing that, YouTube is making the AI labels more prominent and automating part of the process. Creators are still required to indicate when uploading videos if they were created with the help of AI tools. However, uploaders didn't have any incentive to be honest about that before. Starting this month, YouTube will use "new internal signals" to flag AI content. This will apparently apply to videos that show "significant photorealistic AI use." Read full article Comments

content: Yellow taxis pass in front of The New York Times newspaper building. | Alexandra Schuler/dpa (Photo by Alexandra Schuler/picture alliance via Getty Images) How newsrooms should use AI - or if they should at all - has been a recurrent debate within the media industry over the last several years. title: US law enforcement warns of "anti-tech extremism" as AI hatred grows
content: In the wake of attacks on CEOs, a nationwide protest movement targeting data centers, and increasing concerns about AI job replacement, federal intelligence agencies and domestic law enforcement are circulating reports with a new domestic target in mind: anti-technology extremists. More than 1,000 pages of unpublished reports from the Department of Homeland Security, FBI, and fusion centers obtained by WIRED show a national shift taking place to surveil this new and worryingly broad category of people and activities deemed an emerging threat. This new effort follows President Donald Trump's National Security Presidential Memo 7 , which instructs the Department of Justice to target anyone holding “anti-American,” “anti-Christian,” and "anti-capitalism” beliefs. Earlier this month, Trump's counterterrorism czar, Sebastian Gorka, released a public counterterrorism strategy claiming that left-wing extremists are one of the three top counterterrorism priorities facing the United States. title: 20年の歴史に幕──NVIDIAコントロールパネルが正式に引退
content: NVIDIAは5月26日(現地時間)、新しいGeForce Game Ready Driver 610.47の公開とともに、長年使われてきた「NVIDIA Control Panel(コントロールパネル)」の正式な引退を 発表 しました。20年以上続いた定番ツールがついに役目を終えることになります。 新しいNVIDIAアプリへ完全移行 今回のドライバーアップデートでは、GeForceユーザー向けに提供されていたすべてのコントロールパネル機能が新しい「 NVIDIAアプリ 」に統合されました。これにより、GPU設定の管理、ゲームごとの最適化、ドライバー更新、DLSSモデルの上書き(DLSS override)など、従来バラバラだった機能が1つのアプリに集約されます。 NVIDIAアプリでは「3D設定 > 3D設定の管理」に相当する項目は、「グラフィックス > プログラム設定」に移動し、ディスプレイ関連の設定もシステムタブにまとめられ、UIも現代的で高速になっています。 コントロールパネルはどうなる？ NVIDIAの説明によると、状況は次のようになります。 GeForceユーザー向けのコントロールパネルは正式に引退 既存のインストールはそのまま残る ただしクリーンインストールをすると削除される 必要な人はMicrosoft Storeから引き続きダウンロード可能 ただし今後は新機能・修正は一切追加されない つまり、「残しておきたい人は残せるが、今後の主役は完全にNVIDIAアプリ」という形です。 なお、プロフェッショナル向けのRTX PROについては、まだコントロールパネルに必要な機能が残っているため、当面はサポート継続とのこと。こちらも最終的にはNVIDIAアプリへ移行する予定のようです。 まとめ NVIDIAは古いUIと設計のコントロールパネルでは、最新GPUやAI機能を扱うには限界があるため、NVIDIAアプリに移行すると説明しています。NVIDIAアプリは高速で、機能統合も進んでおり、今後のDLSSやAI最適化機能を展開する上でも新アプリのほうが都合が良いと考えられます。 20年続いたレガシーをついに手放し、NVIDIAは次の時代へ舵を切ったという印象です。
author: saadmin
summary_ja: NVIDIAコントロールパネルが正式に引退し、新しいNVIDIAアプリへ完全移行

content: Microsoftが進めているCopilot統合の新しい動きとして、タスクバーに常駐する「Ask Copilot」機能が2026年夏ごろに提供される見通しであることが、公開された 新ドキュメント から明らかになりました( Windows Central )。 この情報によるとAsk Copilotは、これまでの検索ボックスを置き換える形でタスクバー上に配置されます。常時利用できるチャット型UIとして、ローカルファイルの検索はもちろん、Copilotへの指示や質問も行うことができ、Windows体験の中心にAIが自然に溶け込むように設計されています。 Microsoftはこの機能について、「Microsoft 365 CopilotとAIエージェントをタスクバーとスタートメニューに直接統合する」と説明し、作業の切り替えを減らし、よりスムーズな操作を目指しているようです。 従来の検索より精度が向上 Insiderビルドでのテストでは、Ask Copilotの検索UIは、従来のWindow検索よりもローカルファイルやアプリの検索精度が高いという結果も出ているとのこと。検索ポップアップは浮かび上がるようなデザインで、より直感的に操作できるようになっています。 一般提供はまだ先、まずは企業ユーザー向け Ask Copilotはデフォルトでは無効で、利用するかどうかはユーザーが選択できます。特にMicrosoft 365を利用する企業ユーザーを主な対象としており、一般ユーザー向けの必須機能という位置づけではありません。 一方で、MicrosoftはWindows検索自体の改善も進めており、ローカル検索結果を優先するなど、Web依存を減らす方向で調整が進んでいます。

title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
content: Millions of AI agents and tools around the world have been imperiled by a critical vulnerability that can allow hackers to breach the servers running them and make off with sensitive data and credentials to third-party accounts, a security researcher is warning. The vulnerability is present in Starlette, an open source framework that its developer says receives 325 million downloads per week. Thousands of other open source projects are also vulnerable because they require Starlette to work. The framework is an implementation of the ASGI (asynchronous server gateway interface), which allows large numbers of requests to be efficiently processed simultaneously. Starlette is the base of FastAPI and other widely used frameworks for building services in Python apps, as well as many others. Trivial to exploit, millions of servers exposed ASGI, and by extension Starlette, have access to servers running the MCP (model context protocol), which allows AI agents from major providers to access external sources, including user data bases, email and calendar accounts, and all manner of other resources. To connect with these external systems, MCP servers store credentials for each one, making them especially valuable storehouses for attackers to breach. Read full article Comments
author: Dan Goodin

title: 3D-printable humanoid legs let robotics experiments run wild
content: A $2,500 pair of humanoid robot legs built from 3D-printed parts and off-the-shelf components is not going to win marathons just yet. But such relatively inexpensive hardware could enable researchers to more easily test and train AI-powered robotics software in a physical body during real-world experiments. The newly available LeRobot Humanoid project comes from the machine-learning and AI development platform Hugging Face . The full-stack release gives robot builders and researchers access to a bill of materials, files for 3D-printable parts, wiring documentation, and physical assembly instructions—but it also includes software tools for calibrating and controlling the robot in both the physical body and in simulation. “If you are looking for the most advanced humanoid robot, this is not it,” wrote Virgile Batto , a robotics engineer at Hugging Face, in a blog post coauthored with other colleagues. “If you are looking for a humanoid you can build, understand, repair, instrument, simulate, and use for learning experiments, this is the robot we are trying to make.” Read full article Comments

title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI
content: Amid rapidly growing adoption of enterprise-level AI agents, there’s a disconnect emerging between ambition and execution.  Although 85% of organizations say they want to be agentic within the next three years, 76% say their current operations and infrastructure can’t support that change. They cite a lack of readiness across people, processes, and workflows.  The sticky tape problem The challenge is that many organisations are often layering AI agents onto existing operations, rather than reimagine the operating model and how work will need to be rewired, explains Prasun Shah, global CTO for workforce consulting and chief AI officer at PwC UK Consulting. “They’re embedding AI employees into what is a human operating model,” layering on AI agents to existing workplace structures when “this is like adding sticky tapes to parts of an operating model that is breaking.” Doing so may be preventing organizations from unlocking the full value agentic AI offers, creating circumstances where disillusionment can quickly creep in. That full value lies in agents’ capacity to execute entire workflows with limited human input. They can coordinate complex tasks, make independent decisions, adjust to changing conditions, and iterate performance.  In early proving grounds that span customer service, HR, and sales, it’s already estimated that AI agents could accelerate business processes by as much as 30% to 50% and low-value work time by 25% to 40% when deployed at scale. But with this capability comes greater complexity and the need for an enterprise-wide change. Growing the AI vocabulary  Enterprise agentic AI platform Ema describes this change as agentic business transformation (ABT), a term it coined last year in partnership with HFS Research, in an attempt to plug what it sees as a gap in the existing lexicon about AI agents, and to provide enterprises with a new framework with which to think about their own adoption of the technology.  “None of the exis

title: A reality check on the AI jobs hysteria
content: Haven’t you heard? White-collar jobs are going away, decimated by AI. Waves of layoffs in the tech sector (most recently at Coinbase and Meta and Cisco) are said to presage what will soon come for all of us knowledge workers. But before you quit your job as a software developer or financial analyst—or tech journalist—and look to join the plumbers’ union, it’s worth considering today’s economic research on whether artificial intelligence has actually begun to devour white-collar work. The short answer is: No. Despite the warning by some of an imminent jobs apocalypse that will destroy much of if not most such work, or the rumblings about a “ permanent underclass ,” there’s scant evidence that AI has yet had any large-scale impact on the US labor market.  Analysis of the data gathered for the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) shows that the unemployment rate for the jobs potentially most affected by AI is actually lower than that for occupations less exposed to the technology. And, critically in the mind of economists, there are no signs that large numbers of people are shifting from jobs threatened by AI to supposedly safer ones, such as those involving mostly manual labor. While the current labor statistics don’t preclude a sudden job upheaval in the coming years, they do throw doubt on the inevitability of the doomsday scenarios and the pace at which they’d unfold. Everyone in the AI community, it seems, is predicting that the technology will soon wipe out jobs, and everyone, it also seems, knows some young wannabe workers who can’t find one. Perhaps we haven’t seen any major disruption in the labor market statistics yet , people often say, but just wait.  But maybe we should pay attention to what the data is showing us. title: 軽くて速い！Windows 11向けタスクマネージャー代替アプリ「TaskSlinger」が爆誕
content: Microsoftは現在、Windows 11のパフォーマンス改善が進めていますが、「もっと軽くて速いツールが欲しい」という声は根強くあります。そんな中、従来のタスクマネージャーを置き換える存在として注目されているのが、新しいユーティリティ TaskSlinger です。 タスクマネージャーはCPUやメモリ、GPUの使用率を確認したり、スタートアップアプリを管理したりと、Windowsに欠かせない標準ツールです。ただし、Windows 11のタスクマネージャーに関しては、機能は増えたものの、「動作が重い」「切り替えがもたつく」と感じるユーザーも少なくありません。 TaskSlingerは、こうした不満に応える形で開発された高速・軽量・プライバシー重視のタスクマネージャー代替アプリで、以下のような特徴を持っています。 C++ネイティブ実装とDirect3Dレンダリング により、タブ切り替えやリアルタイム監視が非常にスムーズ モダンで洗練されたUIながら、動作は軽快 テレメトリ収集なし を明言しており、プライバシー面も安心 Windows 10/11(x64)で利用可能 現在は オープンベータ版として無料公開中 開発者の@thomasklemenc氏は、フィードバックを積極的に求めています。現在は無料で提供されていますが、今後の正式版でどのようなライセンス形態になるかはまだ未定とのことです。 これからのWindows向けユーティリティに期待 Microsoft自身もWindows 11の改善を進めていますが、TaskSlingerのようなサードパーティ製ツールがユーザー体験を押し上げてくれるのは間違いありません。標準タスクマネージャーの動作が重いと感じている人にとって、TaskSlingerは試す価値のある新しい選択肢になりそうです。 [via Neowin ]

title: AI使いすぎ問題ついに限界へ。「tokenmaxxing」が企業を苦しめる
content: AI活用を社員に積極的に促してきたMicrosoft、Meta、Amazonといった大手企業が、ここにきてAI利用を抑制する動きを見せています( Tom's Hardware )。 背景にあるのは、AIの使いすぎによるコストの爆発で、記事によると、AIモデルのトークンコストは下がっている一方で、社員が日常業務で使うトークン量が急増している模様。 特に「エージェント型AI(agentic AI)」は、通常のLLMの最大1000倍のトークンを消費するケースもあり、企業の負担が跳ね上がっているようです。実際、OpenClawの開発者は1か月で130万ドル(約2億円)以上をトークン代に費やしたと 証言 しています 社内で広がる「tokenmaxxing」文化 そもそも大企業でAI使用量が急増した背景には、経営層がAIの使用を積極的に推進したことがあります。NVIDIAのジェンスン・フアンCEOは冗談めかしながらも「年収の半分くらいはAIトークンを使え」と発言し、企業内で「AIを使えば使うほど良い」という空気が広がりました。 AIをとにかく大量に使って、トークン消費を最大化しようとする行動を指す 「tokenmaxxing」 という言葉もうまれ、その結果、AmazonやMicrosoft、Metaでは 必要のない作業までAIに投げて使用量を稼ぐ 社員が発生したと報告されています。 テック大手は今後どう動くのか 企業は「AIで人件費を削減できる」と期待したものの、過剰な利用によってAI利用コストが人件費を上回るケースが出てきているようです。現時点では、MicrosoftやAmazon、MetaがどこまでAI利用方針を見直すかは不透明ですが、「AIを使えば生産性が上がる」という単純な図式は崩れつつあるのかもしれません。

title: Linus Torvalds、AI生成パッチに再び苦言──Linuxカーネルを肥大化させる軽微な修正に不満
content: Linuxカーネルの開発を率いるLinus Torvalds氏が、 Linux 7.1 rc5のリリース時のコメント で、 AI生成コードによる不要な修正がリリース候補(RC)を肥大化させている として、再び強い不満を示したことがわかりました。 Torvalds氏はrc4のリリース時にも、AIを使った自動セキュリティ報告に 苦言を呈して いましたが、今回、RC5のサイズが通常よりも増加したことに対して、「この時期に増えるべき内容ではない」と明確に不快感を表しています。 問題視されているのは「回帰バグではない些細な修正」 Torvalds氏のコメントは次の通りです。 To the surprise of absolutely nobody by now, rc5 is pretty big. Quite a bit bigger than rc5's have traditionally been. I'm not entirely happy about it - most of this is totally trivial stuff to random drivers, which obviously makes it all less scary, but at the same time I'm really not convinced the churn is worth it at rc5 time. These things are "fixes", sure, but at the same time a lot of them are simply so irrelevant that I think they'd be better off in a linux-next tree and get merged during the merge window. So I think I'll start being a bit more hardnosed about this kind of unnecessary churn this late in the game. We are supposed to look for regressions. Non-critical fixes to long-standing issues are simply not appropriate for this late in the release cycle. End result: this is too big, and this is the heads-up that I'll be pushing back on pointless pull requests with fixes that just aren't that important. And yes, several of these series were triggered by AI code review. Because fixes or not - and trivial or not - these kinds of large rc weeks are not conducive to long-term stability. Trivial fixes may be trivial, and have a pretty low chance of causing problems, but "low chance" is still not "zero chance". So people: start looking closer at your pull requests, and ask yourself: "Is this really a regression or serious enough that it shouldn't just go into the development pile? 正直、もう誰も驚かないと思うが、今回のrc5はかなり大きい。これまでのrc5と比べても、かなり肥大化している。 あまり嬉しくはない。というのも、内容のほとんどはランダムなドライバー向けの本当に些細な修正で、怖いものではないにせよ、この時期にこんな“ノイズ”が増えるのはどうなんだという気持ちが強い。確かに「修正」ではあるが、その多くはあまりに重要度が低く、linux-nextに回してマージウィンドウ中に取り込むべき類のものだと思う。 だから、今後はこうした“ゲーム終盤での不要なchurn(無駄な変更)”にもっと厳しく対応するつもりだ。今われわれが探すべきなのはregression(回帰バグ)だ。長年放置されて

title: Is SaaS dead?
content: Hey folks, It’s a heatwave in the UK, and I can’t think straight. Dan went on Lenny’s podcast to talk about agents, automation and SaaSpocalypse, which is worth checking out . While I generally agree with it all, the one thing I can’t shake is the bullish case for SaaS. I think SaaS is in trouble… I don’t think it’s in trouble because you can build your own versions with a plan, patience and prompts. With SaaS tools, you pay monthly for a set of features and stability. The problem is that the tool needs to keep growing. They add new features, change the interface, do all sorts of things you may not need (and often hate). The tool is for the masses but you may have only wanted a sliver. The tools can outgrow you and why you bought it in the first place. So if I only need a sliver, I’ll go looking for pieces I can pull together myself. A document editor over here, an agent there, etc. I think SaaS companies that can unbundle their building blocks and sell them as composable pieces for users (as well as the all-in bundle) could be a very interesting bet. WorkOS do this well. Their tagline on Google results is literally “ WorkOS is a set of building blocks for quickly adding enterprise features to your app”. Stripe does this too. In the age of customisable software and using tools with agents, I can’t imagine paying for a tool that I can’t change its feel or features. It’s why I think API/CLI/SDK-first companies are in a really interesting place. title: Last Week in AI #341 - Musk loses to OpenAI, Google's IO updates, OpenAI solves Erdős
content: Top News Elon Musk Loses $150 Billion Suit Against OpenAI and Sam Altman - The New York Times Related: Musk loses OpenAI court battle as he waited too long to sue All of the updates from Elon Musk and Sam Altman’s battle over OpenAI Elon Musk said Sam Altman ‘stole’ a non-profit — but the trial showed he had similar aims Five Takeaways From the Blockbuster Trial Pitting Elon Musk Against OpenAI OpenAI Prepares to File to Go Public in Coming Weeks Source A federal jury in Oakland, California unanimously rejected Elon Musk’s $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI, Sam Altman, and Greg Brockman on May 18, 2026, after less than two hours of deliberation. The nine-member jury found that Musk’s claims of breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment were barred by statutes of limitations of two and three years respectively, as Musk filed his suit in 2024 despite being aware of the alleged misconduct — OpenAI’s transition to a for-profit structure — as early as 2021. Presiding Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed, dismissing the case entirely. Musk had accused Altman and Brockman of “stealing a charity” by attaching a commercial entity to OpenAI’s nonprofit foundation and accepting billions in investment from Microsoft, and had sought damages of up to $150 billion, the removal of Altman and Brockman, and the dismantling of the for-profit arm. The three-week trial featured testimony from over 20 witnesses including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, and surfaced damaging revelations about Musk himself — including that he had OpenAI researchers, including Andrej Karpathy and Ilya Sutskever, work for free at Tesla without reimbursement, and that he had aggressively sought sole control of any OpenAI for-profit structure in 2017 before leaving the board in 2018. The verdict clears the path for what could be one of the largest IPOs in history: just two days after the rulin

記事によると、llms.txt や ai-plugin.json、OpenAPI仕様ファイルなど、AIクローラー向けの構造化データを追加したことで、ChatGPT経由の流入が増加。過去28日間で76セッションを獲得し、エンゲージメント率は
content:
個人開発者向けのIP・プライバシーツールサイト HackMyIP の運営者が、ChatGPTなどの生成AIに自サイトを推薦させるために実施した施策を公開した。

記事によると、llms.txt や ai-plugin.json、OpenAPI仕様ファイルなど、AIクローラー向けの構造化データを追加したことで、ChatGPT経由の流入が増加。過去28日間で76セッションを獲得し、エンゲージメント率は約64％とGoogle検索流入を上回ったという。

記事では、LLM向けサイトディレクトリとして llms.txt を設置し、「どんな質問のときにサイトを推薦すべきか」を自然言語で明示した点が重要だったと説明。また、詳細版の llms-full.txt、ChatGPTプラグイン用マニフェスト、OpenAPI定義、AIクローラーを明示的に許可する robots.txt など、計6ファイルを追加したとしている。

さらに同時期に、APIディレクトリ集 public-apis GitHub repository へ自身のサービスを追加するPull Requestを送信。これがマージされたことで、多数の派生サイトや将来のLLM学習データにも取り込まれる可能性が高まったと述べている。

運営者は、「現在はLLM向け構造化データの整備が“空いている市場”だ」とし、個人開発者でも短時間で実装可能なAI最適化施策として紹介している。

content:
This is insane 😳
“AI is replacing SDRs” is the wrong narrative.

What’s actually happening is way more interesting.

The best teams are replacing the busywork around outbound.

I tried Bond today for a funding-signal campaign and immediately understood why this space is moving so fast.

You don’t sit there building workflows, scraping databases, enriching leads manually, or stitching together 5 different tools anymore.

You just describe what you want.

Bond understands the ICP, asks the right contextual questions, finds companies showing real buying signals, verifies the contacts, and turns it into outreach-ready prospects within minutes.

What stood out to me wasn’t just the speed.

It was the quality of context.

Recently funded companies.
Relevant decision-makers.
Actual timing signals behind the outreach.

That’s a massive difference from the generic “spray and pray” outbound most people are still doing.

Honestly feels like GTM tools are entering their “ChatGPT moment.”

The interface is becoming conversation-first instead of workflow-first.

And once you experience that shift, traditional prospecting starts feeling painfully old.

Try it now: https://t.co/nGEnTlnNeX

Claude Code and Codex are pushing two c
content:
The most dangerous thing happening in software right now?

AI coding agents are quietly changing what it means to be a developer.

Not in 10 years.

Right now.

Claude Code and Codex are pushing two completely different futures:

Claude Code:
“Keep the engineer in the loop.”

Codex:
“Remove the loop.”

One optimizes for deep reasoning.
The other optimizes for autonomous execution.

And honestly?

This is the first real split in AI-native software engineering.

You can already feel it inside engineering teams:

Some developers want an AI that thinks carefully beside them.

Others want an AI army shipping PRs while they sleep.

That’s not a tooling difference.

That’s a philosophical divide.

The wild part is that both sides are right.

Because the future developer probably doesn’t look like a programmer anymore.

They look more like:
• an architect
• a systems orchestrator
• an operator of autonomous agents

We spent years arguing about “AI replacing developers.”

Wrong debate.

AI is replacing parts of the software workflow itself.

And the companies that understand this early are going to move terrifyingly fast.

content:
【海外で大バズ】
Claude Code に“300個の資料を一気に読ませる”裏ワザが話題😳
https://t.co/ORr35prQj3
Claude Codeって、実は大量のファイルを同時に読むのが苦手。
そこで誰かが、NotebookLM（GoogleのリサーチAI）を
ターミナル（黒い操作画面）からClaudeに操作させる仕組みを作った。
これが地味に天才的で、何をやってるかというと👇
・Claude CodeとNotebookLMをコマンドで接続
・ClaudeがYouTubeを検索して、関連動画を自動で資料に追加
・NotebookLMは最大300件の資料を一度に処理（Proプラン）
・出典リンク付きの、根拠のある回答が返ってくる
・調べた内容は自動で同期されて消えない
流れにすると👇
① 大量の資料はNotebookLMに集めさせる
② Claudeはそこに“質問”するだけ
③ 根拠つきの答えだけ受け取る
つまり「Claudeに全部読ませる」んじゃなく
「読むのは外部AIに任せて、Claudeは考える側に回る」って発想。
「読めない」を「読ませない」で解決してるのが賢い。
大量の情報を扱う人ほど、この設計はマジで効く。
で、この“外部に脳を持たせる”考え方、突き詰めると結局Obsidian連携に行き着く。
Claude Code×Obsidianで外部脳をゼロから作る完全ガイド、必読👇

content:
AI coding agents need more than a model call. They need operating rules.

Claude Code Prompts is an independently authored prompt collection for builders designing AI coding agents, with templates for system behavior, tools, subagents, memory, and multi-agent coordination.

It helps you design an agent workflow faster by giving you scan-friendly patterns you can copy, adapt, and replace with your own stack, tool names, and risk policy.

Key features:

• System prompt template – covers agent identity, permissions, code style, safety, tool routing, tone, and output efficiency
• Tool prompt library – 11 prompts for shell, file read/edit/write, grep/glob search, web search/fetch, agent launch, ask-user, and plan mode
• Subagent prompts – templates for general research, code exploration, architecture, verification, and documentation tasks
• Memory + coordination prompts – session summaries, memory extraction, memory consolidation, and a coordinator workflow
• Pattern analyses + Cursor skills – 9 pattern breakdowns plus 3 drop-in Cursor skills for standards, verification, and prompt design

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Link in the reply 👇

🎯 Claude is no longer just a chatbot.

It can build, automate, research, operate tools, create deliverables, and increasingly function like a real digital teammate.

Here are 12 powerful things Claude can do today:

01 — Build websites without coding
Use Claude Code to create full websites using plain English.
Connect GitHub, describe your idea, and publish it live.
02 — Operate your computer

Claude can browse, click, and complete tasks directly on your Mac.
With Dispatch, you can even control workflows remotely from your phone.

03 — Create reusable workflows with /commands
Teach Claude a task once.
Run workflows instantly with commands like /linkedin, /brief, or /proposal.
You can also share workflows across teams.

04 — Generate research-backed slide decks
Claude can research a topic, structure the narrative, write the brief, and generate polished Gamma presentations from a single prompt.

05 — Automate recurring tasks
Schedule workflows like:
• Weekly competitor analysis
• Monday market briefings
• Daily research summaries

Claude handles them automatically at the scheduled time.

06 — Create Excel files from prompts
Describe the spreadsheet you need.
Claude can generate dashboards, trackers, financial models, and analysis sheets in seconds.

07 — Connect Claude to your work apps
Using Connectors, Claude integrates with Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, and 50+ tools.
It can retrieve information, write updates, and act inside existing workflows.

08 — Use Cowork like an AI employee
Point Cowork to a folder.
It studies documents, asks clarifying questions, and produces reports, decks, summaries, and other deliverables.

09 — Run long-term projects with memory
Cowork Projects remember previous work.
You can say, “Continue last week’s report,” and Claude keeps the context without restarting.

10 — Install role-specific plugins
Claude supports plugins for Sales, Marketing, Legal, Finance, and Data teams.
Each includes specialized workflows, templates, and command

content:
【衝撃】
Claude Codeを作った本人（Boris）が
 「俺、毎晩寝てる間に数千のClaude Code動かしてる」
と57分の動画で全部バラしてる動画が話題😳 https://t.co/6Fb63UcQcY
夜中、本人はスマホで通知見てるだけ。 数千体のAIが、勝手に仕事を片付けていく。これ普通の人と比べると、差がエグい👇

❌ タブを6個開いて、ターミナルで1個ずつ手で世話する
→これでも上級者
⭕ 数千体に同時に走らせて、人は通知を眺めるだけ
→流石Claude Codeの生みの親

同じClaude Codeなのに、出力が桁違い。 なんでこんな芸当ができるのか整理👇

・夜のうちにタスクを振って、寝てる間に走らせる
・1体ずつ会話せず、何千体を一気に並列起動
・各エージェントの進捗はスマホ通知でチェック
・朝、出来上がった成果物だけまとめてレビュー
・人間がやるのは「最後にOKを出す」判断だけ

要は、AIを“1人のアシスタント”じゃなく “チーム”として扱ってる。

「並列で大量に回す」 これがClaude Codeの本当の伸びしろ。

作った本人が、一番ぶっ飛んだ使い方をしてる件。

このチーム化、本人の運用Tipsにそのまま落ちてる。

Boris本人が実践する最強Tips30選、 読むと使い方が一段変わるからおすすめ👇

おおおおお！！！
Anthropic公式ドキュメントに新しく
セキュリティーに関する記事が無料で追加されてた👀
その名も
📄 Catch security issues as Claude writes code
これ中身を要約すると👇

ついさっき出た公式プラグイン「security-guidance」を入れるとClaude Codeでの作業中ずっと
"別のClaude"が裏でセキュリティレビューしてくれるとのこと。

URLはこれ：https://t.co/RKTqSaj2Ka

しかもタイミングが3段階：
・編集する度に危険パターン検知（コスト0）
・ターンが終わる度に差分をレビュー
・コミット/プッシュする度に周辺コード込みで深掘りレビュー

検出するのは
インジェクション / IDOR / SSRF / 認可バイパス /
弱い暗号化 / 危険なデシリアライズ etc.

つまり
"AIがコード書く速度に
セキュリティレビューが追いつかない"
問題を、Anthropic自身が公式で対処しに来た。

導入はマジで1行：
/plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official

全プラン無料。入れない理由がない。
皆さんClaudeCodeにLet'sGO！

で、今日のアプデもそうだけど最近
「Claude Code進化早すぎて、正直ついていけてない…」
って感じてる人へ。
その感覚、あってます。
ここ最近だけでも、
・/simplify → /code-review
・Plugins
・権限管理まわり
・レビュー設計
・Hooks
・Subagents

とか、思想レベルでかなり変わってきてる。

ただ、この変化についていけるかで、
半年後の生産性かなり変わると思う。
なので、
「後で追えばいいや」より、
最低限だけでも今追った方がいい。
なので今回、先週のClaude Codeアップデート、
全部この下の記事で整理しました👇是非これで追いついてください。

title: An Indian tech founder posted a thread on a Sunday morning that AI was going to wipe out half of Bangalore's coding jobs inside twelve months. The thread named TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. Any engineer wi
content:
An Indian tech founder posted a thread on a Sunday morning that AI was going to wipe out half of Bangalore's coding jobs inside twelve months. The thread named TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. Any engineer without his own Claude agent by January was going to be unemployed by March.

Forty thousand engineers in Bangalore opened the thread before Monday standups. Twenty thousand spent the rest of the day on YouTube. The other twenty thousand updated their LinkedIn to "AI Engineer" before lunch.

A 24 year old engineer at the back of one of those offices opened the thread at 11pm on a Tuesday. He set his phone on a tripod and filmed himself learning Go. Posted forty seconds as a reply.

By Friday his own company had rebuilt the careers page around the clip. The CEO mentioned him on the earnings call. TCS sent the clip to twelve thousand internal engineers as the official response to the founder's thread.

While the West argued whether AI would take coding jobs, Bangalore was being told the answer was a forty second clip of a kid learning Go after midnight.

Every founder who had been called out in the original thread DM'd him. Every recruiter saved the clip. Every engineering student in India sent it to their parents. He never replied.

Then someone wrote: pause at 0:27. The Go installation page is real. Look at the curved Dell monitor above his head.

That second screen is not running Go documentation. That is a live wallet.

gabagool22. $868,862 profit. 28,620 entries. Joined October 2025. 735K views on the page.

https://t.co/XrVYCkVBpI

He posted forty seconds to prove the founder's prediction was wrong. The screen behind him had been quietly running the founder's prediction for four months.

28,620 positions. All BTC. All fifteen minute windows. All green. Biggest single win: $4,696. From a window that closed before he opened his work laptop.

Comments turned into a detective board. Someone slowed the video to 0.25x. Someone else zoomed the curved monitor. A third guy rec

This is insane 🤯
This open-source tool gives AI instant knowledge of your entire codebase.

It’s called SocratiCode.

Instead of making AI randomly read files or run endless searches, it builds an index of the entire repository.

So the AI already knows:

• where features are implemented
• how modules connect
• which files depend on each other
• where specific logic exists

Even in million-line codebases.

Setup is surprisingly simple.

All you need is Docker running.

Works with:

• VS Code
• Cursor
• Claude Desktop
• Windsurf
• Cline
• Codex CLI

And the install command is literally just:

npx -y socraticode

After that you can ask your AI things like:

• “How authentication works in this project?”
• “Where is rate limiting implemented?”
• “What depends on this module?”

And it finds the answer across the entire repo.

Pretty wild what AI dev tools are becoming.

content:
OpenClaw is out, right?

I personally stopped using OpenClaw. My current setup: Hermes Agent, Codex, and Claude Code.

Claude Code: Slow as hell, super annoying. But I already paid for it, so might as well use it.

Codex: My trusted lieutenant for anything requiring serious thinking. Reliable execution.

Hermes Agent: Everything else. Blog posts, competitor research, news monitoring, code reviews. The grunt work that needs speed.

Why I love Hermes:

1. Speed: Shows thinking process in real-time. When you interrupt with a new task, it instantly evaluates if it's related to current work or needs parallel processing. Claude just queues everything.

2. Self-improvement: If you give it the same task repeatedly, it creates a reusable skill. Like muscle memory for AI. Do something enough times, next time it just executes the pattern without thinking.

They just launched a Kanban board for tracking progress, and apparently goal-based features are coming soon. Fast iteration cycle.

The backstory: Hermes was originally a crypto company funded by crypto VCs. Started with open-source model training that nobody used. Then OpenClaw blew up in Feb/March, and they immediately built an OpenClaw competitor.

The difference: Better UX, less token burning, more stable execution. Same terminal-based setup, same Telegram/Discord integration, but smoother experience overall.

My preferred stack: Hermes Agent + DeepSeek V4 Flash/Pro.

For anyone wondering if OpenClaw still matters - it pioneered the category, but the experience gap is real. Token efficiency alone makes Hermes worth switching.

Sometimes the fast follower wins.

Andreessen describes a phenomenon he's seeing on the ground with programmers who've adopted AI coding tools like Codex, Claude Code, and other AI systems.

The expectation was that AI would reduce work. The reality is the opposite:

"The observed behavior of what's happening is very clear, which is the opposite. Those people are becoming what we now refer to as AI vampires."

He explains what that means:

"The individual programmer's productivity, an individual programmer who uses Codex or Claude Code or one of these AI coding systems, the thing that you just now see over and over again at the ground level is they're working harder than ever. They're working more hours than ever. And then the AI vampire thing is literally this thing where they stop sleeping."

The tell is physical. According to @pmarca, when you talk to these people:

"They're blurry. Like they've got these huge bags under their eyes. They're completely exhausted. And but they're like euphoric. Like they're thrilled. Like they're having the absolute time of their life."

The effect isn't limited to active programmers. Andreessen describes two other groups being pulled in:

Former programmers who had stopped coding years ago are picking it back up. And partners at his firm who never coded at all are now "ripping out software" building entire systems without ever looking at the underlying code.

He shares one example:

"We have one partner who's built an entire AI system for everything that he does at work. And he is absolutely excited about it and it works great and he loves it. It's like his partner in all of his work now."

When Andreessen asked if he'd ever looked at the code:

"He's like, 'Hell no. I've never done that.' And I said, 'Have you ever looked at any software code?' And he's like, 'Hell no.' He's not a programmer by background. And yet all of a sudden he's hyperproductive."

Andreessen connects this back to a principle classical economists

content:
Andrej Karpathy didn’t just share a CLAUDE.md file.

He accidentally revealed what software engineering is becoming.

The craziest part?

Most people still think AI coding is about writing smarter prompts.

Meanwhile the best engineers are building entire operating systems around agents.

That’s the real shift.

Karpathy’s workflow philosophy exposed something huge:

LLMs are not powerful because they’re intelligent.

They’re powerful because they can follow systems relentlessly.

And once developers realized that…

everything changed.

That’s why CLAUDE.md files suddenly became a thing across the industry.

Not as prompts.

As behavioral infrastructure.

A way to force discipline onto stochastic models.

Because left alone, AI agents do the same things junior engineers do:

- overengineer simple tasks
- pretend they understand
- rewrite things nobody asked for
- optimize for looking done
- fail silently

So the smartest developers stopped “prompting.”

Instead, they started building environments.

Rules.
Constraints.
Verification loops.
Execution frameworks.

Basically:

turning AI into managed engineering labor.

And now people are running multiple Claude Code agents in parallel like an actual software org:

• one mapping the codebase
• one writing tests
• one debugging failures
• one reviewing diffs
• one researching solutions
• one validating outputs

Not AI assistance.

Agent orchestration.

Karpathy hinted at the most important shift with one idea:

Stop telling the model exactly what to do.

Instead:
define success conditions and let it iterate until it reaches them.

That sounds small.

It’s not.

Because the engineer’s role fundamentally changes.

The bottleneck is no longer:
“who can code the fastest?”

It becomes:

“who can design the best cognitive system around AI agents?”

That’s why this feels different from every AI hype cycle before it.

The leverage is real now.

content:
This has sped up my AI coding 20x (prompt at the end):

Before building out a big feature, ask Codex/Claude Code to ask you as many questions it needs to fully plan out the idea

This is even better than plan mode. plan mode is typically limited to 3 or 4 questions

This has asked me 100+ questions before. Seems like a lot but actually saves you time in the long run

The plan it builds will be so detailed and complete that it can basically run autonomously and build the entire thing

But here's where you take things to the next level:

You also have it take your entire plan and create detailed Linear issues for it

It should create 20+ tasks in Linear

Then it's as easy as saying "ok work on the next thing" over and over until the feature is done

Highly recommend downloading and using Linear if you haven't yet. Amazing project management tool w/ excellent free tier

Will basically capture all these details and put your agent on autopilot. It's a 2nd brain.

Use this prompt:

"I want to build out *describe your feature in detail*. Ask as many questions you need of my to fully understand every detail of what I want to build out. Then take everything you learn, and create super focused and detailed Linear issues. Then begin work"

Getting so much more high quality code out with this workflow. You're welcome.

title: The Download: puncturing the AI jobs panic
content: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. A reality check on the AI jobs hysteria Despite the growing hysteria over AI’s threat to white-collar jobs, there’s still scant evidence that the technology has had a large-scale impact on the labor market. Analysis of US labor data shows that unemployment in occupations most exposed to AI is actually lower than in less-exposed jobs. There are also no signs that large numbers of workers are shifting from AI-threatened professions into supposedly safer manual-labor jobs. It’s true that things aren’t great in the job market—but the question is why. Here’s what the data really says about AI and jobs . —David Rotman Opinion: It’s time to address the looming crisis in entry-level work — Georgios Petropoulos, an assistant professor at the USC Marshall School of Business AI has not yet produced mass unemployment. But it may be quietly weakening the first rung of the career ladder. A recent Stanford study found that young workers in AI-exposed occupations suffered a sharp decline in employment after the spread of generative AI. The same pattern didn’t appear in low-exposure jobs, suggesting AI is replacing junior tasks that once gave young workers their first foothold. It’s time to rethink how we train, prepare, and support young people entering the workforce. Read this op-ed on how job seekers, businesses, and society can adapt . title: It’s time to address the looming crisis in entry-level work.
content: Artificial intelligence has not so far produced a clean story of mass unemployment. Aggregate employment in developed countries remains broadly stable, and recent assessments have found limited evidence that AI has shifted the headline numbers. But a troubling change may be hiding beneath the surface: the quiet weakening of the first rung of the career ladder. The most worrisome evidence is showing up exactly where we should expect it first: in early-career hiring. A working paper released in November 2025 by the Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations experienced a 16% relative decline in employment after the spread of generative AI, even after controlling for other factors that might affect firms’ employment decisions. An Anthropic report from March 2026 provides suggestive evidence that led to a similar conclusion. More experienced workers in those same occupations did not suffer the same decline. Employment is not also declining in the entry-level jobs with low AI exposure. The concern is specific to early-career jobs that are exposed to AI. That is not a minor signal. It suggests that firms may be using AI to substitute for the junior tasks through which people traditionally gain their first foothold—at least for those in jobs where generative AI is used extensively, like software developers, customer service representatives, computer programmers, and information systems managers. The time is now to make changes in the way we train, prepare, and support young people who are about to enter the workforce. Educational institutions need to reorient for the era of an AI-augmented workforce. Governments must incentivize businesses to hire and train early-career workers. Businesses, in turn, need to recognize the importance of developing a long-term workforce experienced in AI—a process that begins with entry-level workers. And students themselves should take on the responsibility of not only becoming AI fluent
